client.name: Hearthline
client.cause: Ending fuel poverty for older people in the UK

exampleLines: Nobody should have to choose between heating and eating.
A warm home is not a luxury.

proofPoints: Last winter Hearthline helped 4,200 older people stay warm
£30 covers a week of heating for one household
£75 pays for an emergency boiler repair callout
£150 funds a home energy visit and insulation kit
92% of the people we helped said they felt less anxious about bills
Hearthline has worked in local communities since 2009
complianceNotes: Never show real service users' faces without written consent
Gift Aid statement must appear on every donation page
Avoid implying 100% of donations go to direct services

audience.name: Warm-hearted 45-65s
audience.description: UK adults aged 45-65 with ageing parents, who already give to at least one charity and worry about older relatives in winter
motivations: Wants to protect older people like their own parents
Likes to see exactly what a gift pays for
objections: Worried the money goes on admin
Assumes the government covers heating support

brief.keyMessage: This winter, a warm home for an older person costs less than you think, and right now your gift goes twice as far.

creativeContext.problemInDailyLife: Older people heat one room and tell nobody.
creativeContext.storySeed: My nan heated one room last winter and told nobody.
creativeContext.openingQuestion: When did you last check how warm your mum's house is?
creativeContext.whatWeDo: finds them, fixes the immediate problem and helps them claim the support they are entitled to.
creativeContext.caseStudy: Last winter a retired postman in Leeds was heating his kitchen with the oven door open. A Hearthline home visit fixed his boiler timer, fitted draught excluders and sorted a grant he did not know existed. He told the team he had stopped dreading the postman. Names and details changed to protect privacy; the case is real.

references: Previous winter appeal: best performing creative was a stat-led static with a single older person's hands around a mug

ranked.title: When did you last check how warm your mum's house is
ranked.hook: When did you last check how warm your mum's house is?
ranked.concept: Opens with a question the audience is already half-asking, then widens it to ending fuel poverty for older people in the uk and the £150 ask.
ranked.whyItWorks: A personal question earns the first second of attention without shock imagery.
ranked.audienceInsight: Likes to see exactly what a gift pays for
ranked.visualDirection: Presenter to camera for UGC; for static, the question in large type over a kitchen scene.

ranked.title: Two kitchens, one difference
ranked.hook: Same street. Same week. One kitchen has what it needs. One doesn't.
ranked.concept: A split-frame creative showing two near-identical kitchens: one with what it needs, one without. The only difference is a £30 gift. Copy explains that £30 covers a week of heating for one household.
ranked.whyItWorks: Contrast makes an invisible problem visible in under two seconds, and the £30 price tag answers "what does my money actually do".
ranked.audienceInsight: Wants to protect older people like their own parents
ranked.visualDirection: Split screen of two kitchens, warm vs cold colour grade, one line of copy across the seam, logo bottom right.

ranked.title: The number behind the ask
ranked.hook: £150. That is what it takes: funds a home energy visit and insulation kit.
ranked.concept: A single oversized number fills the frame with a short line underneath: "funds a home energy visit and insulation kit". Supporting line cites: £75 pays for an emergency boiler repair callout.
ranked.whyItWorks: A specific, small number removes the 'drop in the ocean' feeling and makes the ask feel finishable.
ranked.audienceInsight: Likes to see exactly what a gift pays for
ranked.visualDirection: Flat brand background, huge numeral in accent colour, a tight crop of the kitchen in the lower third.

ranked.title: Ride along with the Hearthline team
ranked.hook: We filmed one Tuesday with the Hearthline team. This is what £30 looks like in real life.
ranked.concept: Documentary-style footage of the team doing the work the donation funds (covers a week of heating for one household). No actors, no music swells, just the work.
ranked.whyItWorks: Showing the operation answers the admin-cost worry better than any pie chart.
ranked.audienceInsight: Worried the money goes on admin
ranked.visualDirection: Handheld, natural sound, captions throughout, team in branded jackets, end card with the tier.

ranked.title: Myth: Donation fatigue after Christmas
ranked.hook: "Donation fatigue after Christmas." Here is what actually happens.
ranked.concept: Directly tackles the objection "Donation fatigue after Christmas" in the first line, then explains the gap Hearthline fills and what £75 does about it.
ranked.whyItWorks: Naming the objection first earns trust and pre-empts the scroll-past.
ranked.visualDirection: Text-first creative: objection struck through, answer beneath, presenter to camera for video.

ranked.title: Thirty seconds from our director
ranked.hook: I run Hearthline. I want to tell you exactly where your £75 goes.
ranked.concept: A single unedited take of the charity director speaking plainly about the weeks ahead and the offer. No b-roll, captions only.
ranked.whyItWorks: Low production, high trust. Direct accountability answers the admin objection head on.
ranked.visualDirection: Phone camera, eye level, office or depot background, burned-in captions, 9:16.

ranked.title: From your gift to an older person
ranked.hook: What happens in the first two days after you give £75?
ranked.concept: A three-step explainer: you give, we act, an older person gets what they need. Each step shows the real person or system involved, ending with "pays for an emergency boiler repair callout".
ranked.whyItWorks: Transparency about process is a direct response to the fear that money disappears into admin.
ranked.visualDirection: Three-panel carousel or 15s animation with simple icons in brand colours, one sentence per panel.

ranked.title: A letter you will not get
ranked.hook: Most people we help never write to thank anyone. This is the letter they would send.
ranked.concept: A handwritten-style letter from an older person describing an ordinary good day, revealed line by line. Signed with a first name only. Closes with the £75 ask.
ranked.whyItWorks: The letter form slows the reader down and rewards attention with emotion rather than shock.
ranked.visualDirection: Paper texture, handwriting font animated as if being written, soft lamp light.
riskFlags: Must be clearly labelled as representative, not a real letter, unless consent exists

ranked.title: Doubled until the deadline
ranked.hook: Every gift doubled by the Ashby Foundation until 31 January.
ranked.concept: A countdown-led creative built around the match offer. £75 becomes £150 and the copy states exactly what that pays for twice over.
ranked.whyItWorks: Match funding is the strongest proven conversion lever in charity paid social; the deadline gives a reason to act today rather than someday.
ranked.visualDirection: Bold accent background, the two amounts side by side with an arrow, deadline date in a sticker element.

ranked.title: Older people in your postcode
ranked.hook: Within two miles of you: older people heat one room and tell nobody.
ranked.concept: Geo-personalised copy by region, with Hearthline's local track record (£75 pays for an emergency boiler repair callout). The ask stays national; the framing feels like a neighbour.
ranked.whyItWorks: Proximity increases perceived responsibility and makes impact feel checkable.
ranked.audienceInsight: Likes to see exactly what a gift pays for
ranked.visualDirection: Map-pin style graphic over a local street at dusk, one kitchen highlighted in accent colour.
riskFlags: Needs region-level ad set split for the personalised line

story.heading: What your gift changes for an older person
story.body: Last winter a retired postman in Leeds was heating his kitchen with the oven door open. A Hearthline home visit fixed his boiler timer, fitted draught excluders and sorted a grant he did not know existed. He told the team he had stopped dreading the postman. Names and details changed to protect privacy; the case is real.

faq.question: How much of my donation goes on admin?
faq.answer: Most of what you give funds direct help: covers a week of heating for one household, pays for an emergency boiler repair callout, funds a home energy visit and insulation kit. Hearthline publishes its accounts every year and we are happy to show you exactly how the appeal money was spent.

faq.question: Why does this matter now, after Christmas?
faq.answer: The need does not stop when the giving season ends; for the people we support it usually peaks in the weeks after. That is exactly why this appeal runs now.

faq.question: Doesn't the government already cover this?
faq.answer: Public support helps, but it does not reach everyone and it rarely covers emergencies. Hearthline fills the gap quickly and helps people claim everything they are entitled to. Last winter Hearthline helped 4,200 older people stay warm

problem.heading: The problem, plainly
problem.body: This winter, a warm home for an older person costs less than you think, and right now your gift goes twice as far. Older people heat one room and tell nobody. Hearthline finds them, fixes the immediate problem and helps them claim the support they are entitled to.

story.heading: What your gift changes for an older person
story.body: Last winter a retired postman in Leeds was heating his kitchen with the oven door open. A Hearthline home visit fixed his boiler timer, fitted draught excluders and sorted a grant he did not know existed. He told the team he had stopped dreading the postman. Names and details changed to protect privacy; the case is real.

faq.question: How much of my donation goes on admin?
faq.answer: Most of what you give funds direct help: covers a week of heating for one household, pays for an emergency boiler repair callout, funds a home energy visit and insulation kit. Hearthline publishes its accounts every year and we are happy to show you exactly how the appeal money was spent.

faq.question: Why does this matter now, after Christmas?
faq.answer: The need does not stop when the giving season ends; for the people we support it usually peaks in the weeks after. That is exactly why this appeal runs now.

faq.question: Doesn't the government already cover this?
faq.answer: Public support helps, but it does not reach everyone and it rarely covers emergencies. Hearthline fills the gap quickly and helps people claim everything they are entitled to. Last winter Hearthline helped 4,200 older people stay warm
